title: Appointment of Judge and Additional Judges in the Calcutta High Court
body_text:
In exercise of the power conferred by the Constitution of India, the President of India, after consultation with Chief Justice of India, is pleased to make the following appointments.
Sl. No. Name (S/Shri) Details 1. Shri Justice Biswaroop Chowdhury, Additional Judge Appointed as a permanent Judge of the Calcutta High Court. 2. Shri Justice Prasenjit Biswas, Additional Judge Appointed as Additional Judges of Calcutta High Court for a fresh term of six months w.e.f. 31.08.2026. 3. Shri Justice Uday Kumar, Additional Judge 4. Shri Justice Ajay Kumar Gupta, Additional Judge 5. Shri Justice Supratim Bhattacharya, Additional Judge 6. Shri Justice Partha Sarathi Chatterjee, Additional Judge 7. Shri Justice Md. Shabbar Rashidi, Additional Judge
***
SB/PN/SK

enrichment.summary: The President of India, acting on consultation with the Chief Justice of India, has appointed Justice Biswaroop Chowdhury as a permanent Judge of the Calcutta High Court. Six other Additional Judges of the Calcutta High Court—Justices Prasenjit Biswas, Uday Kumar, Ajay Kumar Gupta, Supratim Bhattacharya, Partha Sarathi Chatterjee, and Md. Shabbar Rashidi—have been given a fresh six-month term as Additional Judges effective 31.08.2026.
enrichment.context: Judicial appointments to High Courts in India are made under Articles 217 and 224 of the Constitution, which empower the President to appoint permanent and Additional Judges after consultation with the Chief Justice of India, the Governor of the state, and the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court. Additional Judges are typically appointed for a term not exceeding two years and can be extended or confirmed as permanent judges based on performance and vacancy availability, following recommendations processed through the Collegium system. This is a routine administrative notification of individual judicial appointments and term extensions, reflecting ongoing personnel management within the higher judiciary rather than any policy or systemic change.
